summary:
NovaForge is an interactive dashboard and AI copilot for exploring fire-safety and combustion research, with a focus on microgravity. It brings research tables and reference documents into one workspace, where users can build visual dashboards, analyze data, and ask questions in natural language. The copilot selects relevant sources and provides answers with citations, helping users move from scattered information to clearer insights.

The project addresses the challenge of making specialized fire research more accessible and useful. Understanding how fire behaves in space can inform safer spacecraft design and support research with potential benefits on Earth. By combining visual analytics with conversational search—and clearly distinguishing real sources from synthetic demo data—NovaForge helps users explore evidence while keeping its origins visible.
details:
NovaForge is an interactive fire-safety research dashboard and AI copilot developed for the NASA Space Apps 2026 challenge. It helps users explore, compare, and interpret microgravity combustion and fire-safety research. Users can view data in dashboards and ask questions in natural language; the copilot can analyze uploaded tables, search reference documents, create charts, and provide cited answers.

The project aims to make specialized research easier to navigate and to support understanding of findings relevant to fire safety in space and on Earth. It is an exploratory research tool—not a substitute for expert review or a safety certification system. The app combines curated NASA reference material with research datasets, and clearly labels synthetic demo data so it is not mistaken for real experimental results.

The frontend uses Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, ECharts, and Leaflet. The backend uses Python, FastAPI, and LangGraph, with Azure Cosmos DB and language-model and embedding services supported through configurable endpoints. The software is designed to run on a standard computer; it does not require custom hardware.

NovaForge’s creative approach is to combine a customizable, Power BI-style dashboard with a conversational assistant. It can ingest both tables and documents, select relevant sources for a question, and show progress and query details as it works. In designing it, the team considered data provenance, clarity, accessibility, safe AI behavior, privacy, and the need to distinguish verified references from synthetic examples. More project and implementation details are in README.md.
